subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In one-point perspective, where do parallel lines appear to meet?
options: At a single vanishing point on the horizon
questions.explain: One-point perspective has receding lines converging at a single vanishing point on the horizon.

options: Two sets of parallel lines crossing to build darker tone
Dotting the surface to suggest tone
questions.explain: Cross-hatching layers a second set of lines across the first to create darker, denser tone.

questions.q: How are complementary colours defined on the colour wheel?
options: Different tones of the same hue
Colours that sit directly opposite each other
Colours that sit next to each other
questions.explain: Complementary colours are positioned opposite one another on the colour wheel, such as red and green.

questions.q: In a landscape, objects placed at the bottom of the picture usually appear to be in the...
questions.explain: Objects lower in the picture plane normally read as nearer to the viewer, in the foreground.

questions.q: Which set lists the three primary colours?
questions.explain: In traditional art theory the primaries are red, yellow and blue, from which other colours are mixed.

questions.q: What is the shading technique of drawing closely spaced parallel lines called?
questions.explain: Hatching builds tone using sets of parallel lines; crossing a second set over them is cross-hatching.

questions.q: Collage is an artwork made by...
options: Sticking different materials onto a surface
questions.explain: Collage assembles and glues various materials, such as paper or fabric, onto a surface.

questions.q: Which medium is a soft, powdery stick available in soft (chalk) or oil form?
questions.explain: Pastels are sticks of pigment, made as soft chalk pastels or richer oil pastels.

questions.q: Which paint is water-based and dries quickly to a permanent finish?
questions.explain: Acrylic paint is water-based, dries fast and becomes water-resistant once dry.

options: A small preliminary model of a sculpture
questions.explain: A maquette is a small-scale model made to plan and test ideas for a larger sculpture.

questions.q: Etching is a printmaking process that uses what to cut into a metal plate?
questions.explain: In etching, acid bites into exposed lines of a metal plate, which then hold ink for printing.

questions.q: Which drawing medium is best for soft, smudgeable, very dark marks?
questions.explain: Charcoal produces rich, dark, easily smudged marks ideal for tonal drawing.
